jobs.title: Software Engineer - Java/Kotlin Senior [Auth]
jobs.company_name: Banco Plata, S.A., Institución de Banca Múltiple
jobs.description:
We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer - Java/Kotlin to join our Auth team — a team that owns authorization for our mobile app Plata and for web, sitting at the intersection of authorization and infrastructure.

Almost everything else depends on this domain working correctly, which makes the job both high-impact and genuinely hard: dozens of internal teams rely on us, requests may require upfront analysis and discovery, and a task that seems straightforward on paper can unveil fascinating architectural challenges once you dive in.

It's the kind of environment where priorities shift and incidents happen — we are looking for someone who can adapt quickly to changing contexts and confidently design solutions, rather than waiting for a fully-scoped plan.

Challenges that await you:

  • Work within our authorization domain, getting hands-on with OAuth2 flows and the AWS infrastructure behind them
  • Handle integrations and feature development for internal consumer teams
  • Clarify requirements with stakeholders, and design the solution
  • Participate in incident response and on-call rotations when things break, to keep our infrastructure robust
  • Build solid, high-quality solutions efficiently in a fast-paced environment
  • Launch new platform initiatives from the ground up as our ecosystem evolves

What makes you a great fit:

  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in a similar position
  • Strong knowledge of one of the JVM languages (Java, Kotlin). Currently, we are using Kotlin, and familiarity with it will be an advantage
  • You have worked with Micronaut, PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka
  • If you're not familiar with Micronaut but work with Spring and its ecosystem — we're looking for you too
  • Comfortable with ambiguity: you can take a vaguely described problem, figure out what's actually being asked, and design a reasonable solution yourself
  • Prior experience in a platform team (rather than pure product development) is a strong green flag — you know what it's like to serve many internal consumers and juggle competing priorities
  • B1 or higher English level for effective communication with an international team

Bonus:

  • Experience leading a non-trivial refactor, spotting architectural problems early, or designing systems in conditions of real uncertainty
  • An interest in eventually working with Go is also a plus

Our technology stack:

Kotlin 2.2 • GraalVM • Micronaut (DI, gRPC) • JOOQ + Liquibase • PostgreSQL • Redis • Kafka • AWS • Grafana + VictoriaMetrics + Micrometer

Our ways of working:

  • Innovative Spirit: A commitment to creativity and groundbreaking solutions
  • Honest Feedback: valuing open, transparent communication
  • Supportive Team: a strong, collaborative community
  • Celebrating Achievements: recognizing our wins together
  • High-Tech Environment: a team full of smart and revolutionary people who date to challenge the status quo of incumbent finance

Our benefits:

  • Relocation support to Cyprus, Georgia or Kazakhstan with full visa & permit support to the employee and family
  • Flexible work from one of our offices or remotely within time zones from GMT+1 to GMT+5
  • HealthcareCoverage
  • Education Budget: Language lessons, professional training and certifications
  • Wellness Budget: Mental health and fitness activity reimbursements
  • Vacation policy: annual leave and paid sick leave as per applicable policies

jobs.title: Director of Underground Explorers Program
jobs.description:
About SPUN

SPUN (Society for the Protection of Underground Networks) is a startup NGO with a mission to map and protect the mycorrhizal fungal networks that regulate Earth’s climate and ecosystems. These fungi draw down approximately 13 billion tons of CO2 each year, yet they have been largely overlooked by science, policy, and practice.

Since our founding in 2021, we’ve built a global data platform to make these invisible networks measurable. Through our Underground Explorers program and network of over 700 Science Associates across more than 80 countries, with the majority in the Global South, we generate high-resolution biodiversity maps and ML-powered tools that integrate mycorrhizal data into climate, conservation, restoration, and land management decisions.

Our work spans laboratory research, data science, and robotics through to locally led field applications, and we’ve begun working with policymakers and restoration practitioners to apply our findings on the ground. With strong backing from leading foundations and growing momentum in international policy circles, we’re now at an inflection point: scaling these efforts across more landscapes, institutions, and countries over the long term.

Location: This is a remote position. You can work from Africa, Europe, North America or South America.

The Opportunity

SPUN is seeking a Director for our Underground Explorers Program (UEP) to lead its strategic direction, growth and success. The Underground Explorers Program is SPUN's flagship grant program supporting researchers and local communities to map mycorrhizal fungal networks in their local ecosystems and advocate for their protection. Our aim is to expand our understanding of mycorrhizal fungal diversity globally using a decentralized science approach that is core to our organization.

You will own the vision, quality, and impact of the program: setting funding priorities each cycle, chairing the review and selection process, and ensuring UEP continues to fund scientifically rigorous, Global South focused, locally-led projects. This position will directly supervise the Grants & Operations Coordinator, who manages the program's day-to-day administration, and the UEP Data & Training Scientist on technical and scientific support to grantees. You will also provide program management support for SPUN’s Ground Truth Collective (GTC), a UEP sub-program that works with local researchers to collect high-resolution data across global restoration projects. You will work closely with SPUN’s Data Science Lead who manages the research collaboration with GTC teams, and collaborate closely with the SPUN’s communications team on grantee storytelling. You will work with SPUN’s CFO on budget and disbursement strategy and the Data team for grantee sequencing support.

We are looking for someone that combines scientific credibility in mycorrhizal ecology or a related field with strong program leadership and people management experience, and who is comfortable representing SPUN externally to funders, partners, and the broader scientific community.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Program Leadership

  • Define funding priorities, geographic and thematic focus areas, and targets each grant cycle, using geospatial tools to identify coverage gaps and underrepresented regions or ecosystems.
  • Set and revise selection criteria in line with SPUN’s mission, including geographic underrepresentation, scientific rigor, feasibility, local-PI requirements, and Global South representation.
  • Own the program budget in partnership with the CFO, including grant sizing, travel grants, and program support costs.
  • Represent the UEP externally to funders, partners, and at conferences and symposia, and contribute to funder reporting and proposals.
  • Identify opportunities to evolve the program model, such as new funding tracks, partnerships, or initiatives building on UEP
  • Constantly revise and improve the Program reach, design and operations based on grantee feedback.

Review and Selection Oversight

  • Chair the internal review committee and oversee recruitment and onboarding of external grant reviewers from the scientific community.
  • Lead grantee interviews and bring final funding recommendations to the Executive Director for sign-off.
  • Ensure the review process is rigorous, fair, and consistent with program values across all applicant regions.
  • Decide, with the review committee, which applications are placed on the waiting list and revisited in the following cycle.

Team and Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Directly supervise the Grants & Operations Coordinator: set priorities, provide regular feedback, oversight of general functions and support their professional growth.
  • Serve as the escalation point for grantee issues beyond the Coordinator’s scope, including sensitive program or financial matters.
  • Partner with the UEP Data & Training Scientist to ensure grantees receive appropriate technical support for sequencing, bioinformatic analysis, etc.
  • Work closely with SPUN’s communication team to design innovative approaches to highlight grantee research across media types.
  • Coordinate cross-functionally with Finance/CFO, and legal to keep the program running smoothly.
  • Extend UEP program management to the GTC sub-program in collaboration with the Data Science Lead, including sub-grant disbursements with the CFO, tracking sampling schedules and sample shipments, and managing the GTC budget.

Program Quality and Grantee Experience

  • Design and continuously improve the grantee experience, including answering special requests from grantees.
  • Track grantees access to program benefits and resolve gaps in delivery.

Program Evaluation and Reporting

  • Analyze program-level data — grantee demographics, geographic and ecological coverage, and scientific output — to assess impact and identify priorities for future cycles.
  • Prepare program updates and impact reports for SPUN’s Executive Director, board, and funders.
  • Work with the Coordinator to ensure the Grantee Tracker and reporting systems support high-quality program evaluation.

What we’re looking for

  • PhD or equivalent experience in mycorrhizal ecology, fungal biology, soil science, or a related field.
  • Experience in program design and/or grants management, ideally within a scientific, conservation, or research-funding nonprofit.
  • Demonstrated experience directly supervising staff and managing cross-functional relationships.
  • Track record of designing, launching, or leading a grant, fellowship, or research-funding program end-to-end.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience working with grantees or partners from different countries and cultures, particularly in the Global South.
  • Comfortable representing an organization externally: funders, partners, conferences, and the media.
  • Fluent in English; proficiency in Spanish or French is a strong plus, given UEP’s grantee base across Latin America and Francophone Africa.
  • Strong commitment to equity and inclusion in science.

Bonus, but not required

  • Experience with GoodGrants, Ramp, or Notion.
  • Hands-on experience in mycorrhizal fungal research, soil biodiversity fieldwork, or environmental DNA methods.
  • Existing relationships within the global mycological, soil science, or conservation research community.

Why Join SPUN

We believe in empowering people to do their best work. This is reflected in our benefits that support health, well-being, growth, and balance. They are tailored to local laws so that everyone across our globally distributed team receives the same high standard of support.

What you can expect:

Health Coverage: 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums covered for employees, plus support for dependent coverage.

Time Off: Flexible PTO with a minimum of 25 vacation days per year that we expect you to take, plus local holidays, sick leave, and wellness days.

Volunteer Days: Paid time each year to contribute your skills and energy to causes you care about.

Wellness Support: An annual health stipend, plus a flexible spending account for US-based employees.

Professional Growth: An annual professional development allowance for your learning, skills, and career progression.

Workspace & Tools: A hardware allowance to get you set up, plus monthly work-from-home and annual workspace allowances so you can work well wherever you are.

Exploration & Connection: Opportunities to travel for fieldwork, retreats, and partner collaborations, bringing our team together in person and closer to the ecosystems we work in.

Birthday Celebration: An annual birthday meal stipend, on us.

At SPUN, we embrace diversity as a fundamental pillar of our mission to protect underground ecosystems. Our commitment to decentralized science depends on the diversity of knowledge and experience on our team and among our partners across the globe. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where all individuals, regardless of their race, ethnicity, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, age, disability, or background, feel valued, respected, and empowered to bring their authentic selves to work. We highly encourage individuals from traditionally underrepresented or marginalized groups, including but not limited to women, LGBTQIA+ people, individuals from the Global South, and individuals with Indigenous heritage, to apply to join our team at SPUN.

To learn more about our organization and culture, please visit our website .

jobs.title: Systems, Knowledge Management & Procurement Officer (Consultancy)
jobs.description:
Position title: Systems, Knowledge Management & Procurement Officer (Consultancy)

Organization : Aflatoun International

Location : Global (consultancy)

Job type : Full time 40 hours

Compensation : Between €2234 and € 2444 per month

Reports to: Director of Finance &Operations

Deadline : 8th December 2026

The Organization

Aflatoun International is a non-profit organization, which offers social, financial & entrepreneurship education to children and young people worldwide, empowering them to make a positive change for a more equitable world. Aflatoun creates high-quality curricula for different age groups, which are contextualized to local needs and circumstances, and are implemented by over 300 partner organizations in 101 countries. Aflatoun programmes inspire children to discover their talents and put them to use, to stand up for their rights and those of their communities through active learning and problem solving. They learn how to save, how to budget, and how to set up social and financial enterprises that benefit themselves, their families and their communities. Aflatoun has been recognized globally (Brookings, Harvard, HundrEd, Million Lives Club) for its high-impact, low-cost model, which has been shown to be effective in changing behaviors of participants across the globe.

By using a social franchise model, Aflatoun transfers curricular content, monitoring and evaluation tools, and training capacity to partner organisations, helping them enhance their existing expertise and create an efficient learning ecosystem. Aflatoun’s programmes follow an active-learning, participant- centered methodology, which combines social and financial education (SFE) through engaging participants, educators, government institutions and civil society organisations.

We are currently looking for a dedicated and enthusiastic Compliance and Administrative officer to join us in our mission.

Position

Aflatoun International has invested significant time and resources in strengthening its internal systems, policies and procedures. The organisation uses several digital platforms to support finance, project management, communications and administration.

The Systems, Knowledge Management & Procurement Officer will help ensure that these systems and processes are well organised, accessible and used effectively across the organisation. The role combines internal systems coordination, knowledge management, procurement administration and practical support to staff.

The Officer will serve as Aflatoun’s internal IT focal point, coordinating support and follow-up with the external IT service provider. Specialist technical work, infrastructure maintenance and technical security services will be delivered by the external provider within the agreed scope of services.

Key Areas of Responsibility

  1. Internal systems and IT coordination
  • Act as the main internal contact for IT-related requests, providing basic user support and referring technical issues to the external IT service provider.
  • Track outstanding issues, follow up on agreed actions and keep staff informed until issues are resolved.
  • Coordinate with the external provider on system maintenance, security updates, backups and recovery arrangements, escalating gaps or concerns to the Director of Finance & Operations.
  • Coordinate user onboarding, changes in access and offboarding, ensuring that access is approved by the responsible manager and updated promptly.
  • Maintain an overview of software subscriptions, licences, service contracts, renewal dates and costs, and identify opportunities to reduce duplication or unnecessary expenditure.
  • Maintain an accurate IT asset register and coordinate equipment purchasing, allocation, maintenance, replacement and return.
  • Coordinate technical support for Microsoft 365, email, domains, website hosting, connectivity and other shared services.
  • Administer the general information mailbox, including routing enquiries and following up with the relevant colleagues.
  • Support the review and implementation of IT policies and staff guidance, working with management and the external provider on data protection and information security.
  • Promote good security practices, including secure sharing, appropriate access permissions and prompt reporting of suspected incidents.
  1. Systems improvement and staff support
  • Review administrative workflows with departments and identify practical opportunities to simplify processes, reduce manual work and improve consistency.
  • Support the effective use of Monday.com, CRM, Exact Online, Microsoft 365, Box and other approved platforms, working with the relevant system owners.
  • Coordinate agreed system changes and improvements with staff, service providers and developers.
  • Maintain clear user guidance and provide induction, refresher training and practical support to staff.
  • Explore appropriate uses of automation and AI to improve efficiency, taking account of confidentiality, data protection, cost and the need for human review.
  • Test proposed improvements with users before wider implementation and follow up on whether they meet the intended need.
  • Document key workflows, system configurations and provider contacts to support continuity and reduce reliance on individual staff members.
  1. Knowledge management and organisational documentation
  • Develop and maintain a practical structure for storing, organising and retrieving organisational information across approved platforms.
  • Agree clear filing, naming, version-control and archiving practices with departments and support their consistent use.
  • Maintain a central register of policies, procedures and guidance, showing the responsible owner, current version, approval date and next review date.
  • Follow up with document owners on scheduled reviews and ensure that approved versions are accessible to the relevant staff.
  • Help departments organise shared resources, templates, manuals and frequently asked questions so that staff can find reliable information easily.
  • Coordinate the documentation and transfer of key knowledge during staff onboarding, role changes and departures.
  • Support teams in recording useful lessons from projects, events and internal processes and making them available for future use.
  • Coordinate the organisation and archiving of legacy files, including Box archives, in line with agreed retention and access requirements.
  • Work with information owners and the external IT provider to ensure that confidential records have appropriate access restrictions.
  1. Procurement and contract administration
  • Prepare purchase orders based on approved requests, ensuring that supplier details, budget codes, amounts and supporting documentation are accurate and consistent in Monday.com and Exact Online.
  • Check that procurement requests meet the requirements of Aflatoun’s procurement policy before they proceed for approval.
  • Review procurement files for the required documentation, including terms of reference, quotations, selection records, approvals and any authorised exceptions.
  • Prepare supplier and non-HR consultancy contracts using approved templates and coordinate their review, signature and filing.
  • Maintain a contract register covering contract owners, deliverables, values, start and end dates, renewal dates and relevant follow-up actions.
  • Maintain the consultant database and records of pre-qualified consultants in accordance with the procurement policy.
  • Track agreed hours, expenditure and remaining contract balances for framework and zero-hour consultancy arrangements, in coordination with the relevant managers and Finance.
  • Provide timely updates to contract owners on approaching expiry dates, expenditure limits and outstanding documentation.
  • Follow up on service evaluations and re-evaluations and ensure that records are complete and accessible to authorised colleagues.
  • Support procurement reporting and audit requests by maintaining complete and traceable records.

Procurement approvals, supplier selection decisions and payment authorisation remain with the designated budget holders and authorised approvers under Aflatoun’s policies.

Non-technical responsibilities as Aflatoun staff

  • Positively contribute to team discussions and the effective running of the organisation;
  • Cross-departmental collaboration, compliance with organisational policies and procedures including submitting monthly timesheets;
  • Promote Aflatoun’s work on social media;
  • Perform other duties and tasks, consistent with the skills and expertise, as required in non-routine circumstances;
  • Be willing to adapt to different tasks and different cross-organisational tasks, this includes but is not limited to helping deliver Aflatoun events such as the International Conferences and staff retreats.

Required Skills & Qualifications

  • A relevant degree, professional qualification or equivalent practical experience in information systems, business administration, operations, knowledge management or a related field.
  • At least five years of relevant experience across internal systems coordination, operations, procurement administration or knowledge management.
  • Experience coordinating external IT providers and following technical issues through to resolution.
  • Practical experience supporting Microsoft 365 and shared digital platforms, including user access, document management and staff support.
  • Experience maintaining procurement records, purchase orders, supplier contracts or consultant databases.
  • Strong organisational skills, attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Analytical and problem-solving skills, with a practical approach to improving processes.
  • Ability to explain systems and procedures clearly to colleagues with different levels of technical confidence.
  • Good interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively in an international, multicultural environment.
  • Sound judgement when handling confidential information and access permissions.
  • Fluent written and spoken English.

Desirable

  • Experience with Monday.com, CRM, Exact Online, SharePoint or Box.
  • Experience developing filing structures, document-control practices or organisational knowledge resources.
  • Familiarity with workflow automation and responsible use of AI tools.
  • Experience working in an NGO or international organisation.

Expected results

  • Staff receive timely support, and issues requiring external IT assistance are tracked through to resolution.
  • User access, equipment, subscriptions and service contracts are accurately recorded and regularly reviewed.
  • Organisational policies and guidance are current, clearly owned and easy to find.
  • Key processes and handovers are documented, supporting continuity when staff change.
  • Procurement and consultancy files are complete, accurate and compliant with internal requirements.
  • Agreed improvements reduce administrative effort and help staff use existing systems more effectively.

Employment details

The position is for a full time. We offer a dynamic and pleasant multicultural working environment, with an indicative gross monthly compensation range of € 2234 and € 2444 per month (inclusive of pension, health insurance, holiday allowance, and national insurance contributions) - the salary level awarded will depend on relevant work experience and educational background.

Due to the nature of Aflatoun’s work with children around the world, specific attention is drawn towards Aflatoun’s Child Protection Policy and its Policy on the Protection of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA). These two policies are required to be signed by new employees and forms part of the employment documents related to the employment contract. The applicant commits to zero tolerance towards sexual exploitation and abuse.

Screening for integrity is part of the recruitment process. Aflatoun considers it important to ensure the reliability, professionalism and the Integrity of its organization and its employees. By applying for this position, the candidate accepts to be screened by Aflatoun which involves conducting a background check with 2 referees from the professional environment of the candidate, submitting a self-declaration of good conduct along with the CV and cover letter, and submitting a declaration of good conduct issued by the Judicial Documentation system in their home country in case they reach the final stage of the hiring process. The screening will cover up to 10 years. Only the data relevant for the screening of the position will be collected. In case the candidate is not selected for the position, the data will be destroyed 4 weeks after the closing of the position.

For technical positions, an additional written test may be required.

Management may appoint at a lower step based on the candidate’s skills and experiences against the position’s requirements

Reaction

Please apply online at

no later than 08/12/2026. If you have any specific, questions on the position please contact the Senior HR Officer Chitra at .

jobs.title: Acquisition Executive (Roblox Games)
jobs.description:
Indigo buys stakes in Roblox games and Fortnite islands and grows them after the deal. Our portfolio is around 600 live games with about 100 million monthly players, and we bring in 20 to 30 new games every month.

As an Acquisition Executive you turn a first conversation with a developer into a signed deal. Our scouts find games and make the first contact. You take it from there: evaluate the game, build the offer, negotiate with the developer, close, and hand the game over to our production team.

What you will do

  • Read a game’s analytics (traffic, retention, monetization) and judge how far it can realistically grow

  • Value the game from its cash flow, then set an opening offer and a walk-away price

  • Negotiate directly with developers, mostly in Discord, and answer their objections honestly

  • Work with our legal team on the contract and get the deal signed

  • Hand the game to production with everything they need to start

What we are looking for

  • A track record of closing deals in sales, business development, M&A or game publishing

  • Comfort with numbers: you can read a dashboard and build a simple cash-flow estimate

  • Clear written English, because most of the negotiation happens in chat

  • Interest in games. Roblox experience helps but is not required: our internal guide takes a new hire from zero

  • Able to run your own pipeline in a fully remote team

Indigo is a fully remote team of 100+ people. You will work closely with the Head of Acquisitions, the scouts and the production team.

Compensation: USD 3,000–6,000 net per month.

Role Title: Optomechanical Design Engineer — Precision CNC Parts (Remote)

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Fully remote

Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $90 -$155/hour

Duration: Initial phase of 20 part packages; production phase to follow

Location: Fully remote, no geographic restrictions

You'll need: 5+ years designing CNC-machined production parts, technical decision authority, and access to parametric CAD software

Your tasks: Author original CAD part packages, and peer review packages from other engineers

micro1 is engaging senior optomechanical and mechanical design engineers to create original CAD part packages for a client project in precision optics and optomechanics. Your engineering judgment is what matters here — no prior AI experience required.

Each package is a new part you design from scratch: a difficult, high-value CNC part with a specific machining challenge, backed by a drawing with full GD&T, a design rationale, and a production scenario you justify from experience. Every part is independently reviewed by three other engineers, and you'll review others' work as well.

What you'll do

  1. Design original parts in parametric CAD, delivered as native files plus STEP.
  2. Produce the technical drawing: dimensions, tolerances, GD&T and datums, material and condition, finish, revision, drawing standard.
  3. Write the design context: intended function, interfaces, operating conditions, the machining challenge, and your material and process rationale.
  4. Build the production scenario: estimated unit cost and drivers, CNC cycle and setup hours, assumed volume, sourcing difficulty and lead time — with the engineering basis for each estimate.
  5. Peer review other engineers' packages against technical quality, production realism, and engineering value, with part-specific evidence for every score.
  6. Revise your own packages against review findings.

What we're looking for

  1. 5+ years of production engineering experience with comparable CNC parts, materials and processes in precision optics or optomechanics.
  2. Technical decision authority: you owned or approved critical design choices — drawing, tolerance or material approval, production release, or enforcing engineering quality standards. Design leads, principal and staff engineers, and technical authorities are the profile.
  3. Experience at OEMs or specialist suppliers whose engineering standards you can reproduce.
  4. Strong GD&T and tolerancing judgment, including cost and inspection implications.
  5. Access to parametric CAD software (SolidWorks, NX, CATIA, Creo or similar) and the ability to deliver native files plus STEP.
  6. Industry experience, not academic.

Important: originality and IP

Every design must be your own original work. You cannot use designs owned by a current or former employer or customer, and you cannot substitute public or purchased CAD. All deliverables become the client's property. If you're currently employed, check your employment agreement regarding outside work and invention assignment before applying.

How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview for this role — it's how your expertise gets in front of the client
  3. Profile review, including evidence of comparable parts and decisions owned
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

jobs.title: Learning & Development (L&D) Specialist - EMEA
jobs.description:
About us

Founded in 1996, Argos Multilingual is a global provider of technology-enabled language, AI and data solutions. We combine human expertise, technology and AI to help organisations communicate, operate and grow across markets.

We work with some of the world’s most recognised companies, from global technology leaders and e-commerce innovators to major organisations in life sciences and manufacturing. Our clients operate at significant scale, giving our people the opportunity to work on complex, high-impact projects.

With 400+ people across 42 countries, cultures and time zones, we are a truly international organisation. We are continuing to expand our capabilities in AI and data alongside our established language and localisation expertise, building on a strong foundation while embracing the opportunities created by new technology.

About the role

Few L&D roles give you the chance to reimagine an entire training library with AI and modern tools. This one does. As our L&D Specialist, you’ll turn fresh ideas into courses people actually want to take, creating learning faster and, above all, building real capability across our workforce. You’ll be one of a two-person L&D team reporting directly to our SVP HR (Head of HR), with real independence and the backing to try new approaches. What you build will shape how hundreds of colleagues learn and grow.

What you'll do

  • Rebuild and modernise our training library with innovative content, recommending what to update, redesign or retire, and drive continuous improvement by tracking industry trends and internal metrics and testing new formats and tools.
  • Plan, organise and deliver training of all kinds, including technical training: build e-learning courses, live sessions, workshops, manuals and knowledge resources in line with the annual L&D plan, and keep them up to date as our tools and processes change.
  • Manage the day-to-day administration of our LMS (currently TalentLMS) and maintain the compliance training matrix, tracking completion and keeping evidence ready for internal and external ISO audits.
  • Coordinate and deliver onboarding training for new hires, and keep improving how we bring people up to speed.
  • Measure impact using models such as Kirkpatrick, run training needs and satisfaction surveys, track L&D KPIs and report clearly to the SVP HR and stakeholders.
  • Manage several training projects at once, building strong working relationships with product owners, managers and subject-matter experts, and coaching internal experts to deliver training well (train-the-trainer).
  • Work closely with the HR team on wider initiatives, such as system implementations and documentation, and take on other related duties as assigned to support HR, L&D and organisational goals.

Skills & Experience

  • 5+ years of hands-on L&D experience in a global organisation, in any industry (technology preferred).
  • Strong experience administering an LMS, LXP or similar platform.
  • Proven experience building e-learning and delivering live training, grounded in learning design principles.
  • Hands-on experience using AI and modern authoring tools to build learning content (for example Articulate 360, Synthesia, Vyond or Camtasia).
  • Comfortable turning learning data into clear reports and insights.
  • Excellent written and spoken English.
  • Nice to have: TalentLMS, ISO compliance training, train-the-trainer programmes or evaluation models such as Kirkpatrick.
  • No localisation experience needed.

Who You Are

  • Dynamic and solutions-driven: you spot what isn’t working, fix it and get things moving.
  • A strong critical thinker who questions how things are done today, learns fast and takes initiative.
  • An owner who takes accountability for your work from start to finish.
  • Great at prioritising: you focus on what matters most and stay organised and detail-minded when plans change.
  • A clear, confident communicator who can influence managers and stakeholders at all levels.
  • Genuinely curious about how AI and new tools can make learning more effective and personalised.
  • Passionate about helping people reach their full potential.

Location

Argos is a remote-first, globally distributed organisation, with offices in seven countries, and we currently hire in 42 countries globally. This is a remote-based role, and you must have the legal right to work in your country. We do not provide sponsorship.

Why Join Us

You’ll be joining Argos at an important point in our growth and transformation. We have almost 30 years of experience and an established global client base, but we’re not interested in simply maintaining what we’ve built.

Our industry is changing rapidly. AI, data and technology are reshaping language and localisation, and we’re embracing that change by investing in new capabilities, exploring new ways of working and continuing to evolve our offering.

As part of a global, remote-first organisation, you’ll work with colleagues across countries, cultures and time zones, with the opportunity to learn from different perspectives and contribute to work with an international reach.

We offer the scale and stability of an established global business, combined with the opportunity to influence how we operate and where we go next. If you want to use your experience, challenge thinking and make a visible contribution rather than simply maintain the status quo, Argos offers the opportunity to do exactly that.

Please check our Privacy Policy to find out more about who is administrator of your personal data after application, purposes and your rights.

jobs.description:
Role Title: Principal Research Scientist (Computer Science / Computational Physics)

Role Type: Contractor (flexible, Part-Time or Full-Time)

Location: Remote

micro1 is engaging Principal Research Scientist (Computer Science / Computational Physics)s to contribute to an advanced customer project at the intersection of computational theory and AI. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters. You will work with frontier AI models and agents to tackle open problems, drive research direction, and define standards for scientific breakthroughs. Your insights and rigorous approach will be pivotal in charting what counts as genuine progress within your subfield.

Scope of Work

  1. Identify, frame, and articulate foundational open problems, theoretical bounds, or simulation challenges where verifiable progress can be demonstrated.
  2. Guide AI models and agents in multi-step research processes—ranging from proofs and algorithms to numerical experiments and high-performance simulations.
  3. Critically assess and validate results, utilizing proof checks, computational reproduction, and formal methods to pinpoint the limits of model-generated reasoning.
  4. Evaluate and document the novelty, correctness, and significance of research outputs relative to current literature and established results.
  5. Produce clear, concise research memos detailing research attempts, partial solutions, and observed model limitations or failure patterns.
  6. Advise on research directions, recommending promising subfields and open problems suitable for advancement via AI models and computational tools.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. 7 - 10+ years of active research in computer science or mathematical/computational physics, with a strong record of scholarly contributions.
  2. Recognition at the field level—such as major prizes, society fellowships, or plenary/invited talks at top scholarly events.
  3. A consistent publication record in leading venues within your domain, with recent results published in the past year.
  4. Demonstrated success resolving named open problems or introducing influential concepts adopted by peers.
  5. Deep, hands-on experience with computational research methods: simulation, numerical analysis, algorithmic implementation, and/or high-performance computing environments.
  6. Proven ability to rigorously examine technical work outside your immediate area of expertise.
  7. Experience on program committees, editorial boards, or with formal research tools (e.g., Lean, Coq, SAT/SMT solvers) is a strong plus, as is a public record of outlining open problems or showcasing research with advanced AI systems.

Health Loft is seeking an experienced, highly independent Senior Paid Search/SEM Manager to take full ownership of our Google Ads and Microsoft Ads programs and drive measurable improvements in patient acquisition.

Paid search is one of our primary patient acquisition channels, and we are looking for someone who can do more than manage campaigns or execute assigned tasks.

- Stay within healthcare advertising policies and privacy-safe tracking practices.

- Experience personally managing or serving as the primary strategic owner of Google Ads accounts spending $200,000+ USD per month.

- Strong experience with Google Ads Search campaigns, Performance Max, and Smart Bidding.

Our mission: We bridge the gap between patients and the life-changing care that registered dietitians provide by strategically growing and delivering innovative medical nutrition therapy nationwide.

jobs.description:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We are seeking a platform engineer to join our Compute Capacity team. This team owns the capacity plan that keeps compute supply ahead of demand across every region we operate in — the forecasting, buffer policy, and provisioning systems that make sure a project never runs into a wall it didn't know was there.

You'll work on the systems that turn a capacity plan into provisioned reality: reservation acquisition, fleet reconciliation, and the automation that keeps what we've committed to in sync with what we're actually running. You'll help build the metrics and alerting that let capacity problems surface months out, on vendor lead time, rather than at the moment someone needs the room.

You'll design, build, and operate systems that are both robust and highly automated — helping us hold the right buffer at the right cost, catch drift before it becomes a shortage, and give every team a single, trustworthy view of how much room we have across the millions of databases we manage.

What You'll Be Responsible For

  • Help build and maintain the capacity plan that keeps Supabase's compute supply ahead of demand across regions and instance families

  • Support buffer policy by modeling headroom targets and their cost tradeoffs for review and sign-off

  • Build and maintain automation that turns the capacity plan into provisioned reality — reservation acquisition and top-up, fleet reconciliation, drift detection between committed and running capacity

  • Extend our infrastructure as code for capacity-relevant provisioning

  • Instrument capacity: build and maintain metrics for saturation, reservation coverage, idle buffer, forecast error, and provisioning latency

  • Build and tune capacity alerting so headroom, quota, and reservation issues surface months out rather than at the moment of impact

  • Support the demand gate — helping intake large customer commitments, launches, migrations, and new regions so they reach the plan before they reach the fleet

  • Contribute to mitigation projects: right-sizing, instance-family migrations, autoscaling improvements, workload consolidation

  • Help drive down compute cost per database through right-sizing, placement, and commitment coverage work

  • Participate in capacity incident response and post-incident follow-through

  • Have production software engineering experience — you've owned and operated a service, not just a notebook. Comfortable in modern languages like TypeScript, Python, and Go

jobs.title: Solution Architecture Manager
jobs.description:
This is an opportunity to run a field engineering team, helping customers understand and implement Canonical's open source solutions in public clouds and in their own data centers. We work across the entire spectrum of cloud offerings, from Ubuntu itself to virtualisation and private cloud, Kubernetes, and the implementation of sophisticated open source solutions such as MLops platforms, data platforms and more. We are rapidly expanding the range of open source solutions we offer and deliver to customers, as we move into new industries like telco, finance, health care and media we design and develop new open source solutions to meet their needs.

We believe that Engineering Managers should be outstanding engineers themselves. They should feel completely at home troubleshooting technical issues and having technical presales conversations with customers. They should contribute to project delivery themselves, but know that the technical contributions they bring are far less significant than their ability to shape the whole team’s direction, focus and delivery. We grow management skills and train engineers, who are interested in soft skills, to be managers.

We believe that open source is just starting to transform the tech sector and enterprise compute. Our goal is to make open source easier, more reliable and more secure for deployment and development. We strive to be the provider of ‘most software to most companies’. To deliver on that ambition, our engineers are carefully selected from the applicants across the globe. We select for brilliance and motivation to take open source to the next level. Our engineering managers help teams achieve more than they realised they could, and feel proud of the result.

Our goal is to build an entirely new level of assurance and observable rigour into the open source supply chain. We have our own estate to monitor, but more broadly our goal is to raise the robustness of the entire global Ubuntu estate through the work of this team.

The Security Operations (SecOps) team is responsible for design, implementation and evolution of Canonical security practices, techniques, tools, systems and policies. The team is the primary owner of strategy and practices that determine how Canonical secures its data, internal infrastructure and build processes. They are responsible for assuring the security and integrity of our own infrastructure and product deployments. They design and implement technical security controls that ensure security threats are automatically identified, contained and remediated. The team will also contribute ideas and requirements for Canonical product security, improving the resilience and robustness of all Ubuntu customers and users subject to cyber attack.

You'll study attack trends across the wider open source software landscape, report findings to internal security teams, and advise the wider engineering community on the best course of action to detect and mitigate possible threats.

As the publisher of Ubuntu, Canonical products are directly or indirectly present in almost every organisation and household in the world, making them a prime target for threat actors. jobs.title: Technical Author (multiple roles and seniority levels)
jobs.description:
Our ambition is to set a standard of excellence in the industry for technical documentation and documentation practice. This is your chance to be a part of that, as a Technical Author at Canonical.

We are building documentation capacity at scale. We have dozens of positions available, for teams and products across the organisation, at all levels from Graduate to Senior Staff.

All applications and candidates are handled through this one entry-point. 

To improve your chances of success in this application, read our advice on how to get a job at Canonical.

These are not traditional technical writer roles. As a Technical Author, you will lead the documentation efforts of a Canonical team, in engineering, business operations or another part of the company. 

You will combine excellence in technical communication with subject-matter expertise and the ability to collaborate with colleagues across the organisation. Even the most junior Technical Authors will have the opportunity to develop and demonstrate technical authority, contributing to documentation practice as a first-class engineering and business discipline.

You will work with the Diátaxis approach to documentation and help elevate standards of technical writing through attention to theory and practice.

The role of a Technical Author

A product-focused Technical Author is a member of a product engineering team, typically focused on a product or family of products. In this role you'll help the team develop documentation that serves the needs of the product's users. You will have responsibility for the quality of the user experience with the product, and will contribute towards the long-term success of the project itself.

A customer-focused Technical Author works in a team such as Field Engineering, Customer Success or Support, dealing with users of complex suites of Canonical software products, sometimes deployed in custom configurations. In this role you’ll take a responsive approach to software documentation problems and develop a strong understanding of how products work together and are used in the real world.

An operations-focused Technical Author is part of a business team, for example Legal, HR or Talent. An important part of this work is to maintain internal documentation, such as employee handbooks. In this role you will help develop and improve materials that hundreds of colleagues rely on daily, and define patterns of business communication for a rapidly-growing organisation.

Some open technical author roles at Canonical

You’ll have a chance to tell us your preferred focus, and we'll work with you to find the right seniority level and team for you.

Whatever your focus, you will also be a part of Canonical's documentation practice team, that includes all the company's Technical Authors. Here, you'll be amongst other documentation experts, who collaborate to define documentation excellence and drive the development of documentation practice and theory, across the company and in the open-source software community.

jobs.title: Performance Engineer - Open Source
jobs.description:
Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1000+ colleagues in 70+ countries and very few office based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.

The company is founder led, profitable and growing.

We have created a new career path at Canonical for Performance Engineers who bring exceptional clarity to software performance, correctness and efficiency. We are adding these roles to every engineering team at the company.

As an open source platform, we have teams that work at every level of the software stack - from the kernel up through server and desktop applications, all the way to the web. We are adding roles with this focus in every engineering team in the company, to act as drivers of performance engineering skills, tools, culture and insights to our entire product range. We have also created a central performance engineering team, where we will drive shared tools, dashboarding capabilities, measurement frameworks, analytical capabilities and skills. We call this career focus 'percorr' because we have found that the same deep insights that enable sophisticated performance measurement and design also enable teams to improve their harnesses and frameworks for correctness. Understanding not only the application, but the runtime, the compiler, and the system, all the way down to the CPU, gives an engineer the ability to think creatively and with insight about the right things to measure, and the right ways to verify correctness. We have found that performance engineers will often improve the deepest and trickiest areas of our test harnesses, and unblock their teams to test and measure previously 'dark' aspects of their work.

We also have teams that work with every major silicon vendor and cloud, with a particular emphasis on performance optimisation of the entire stack for that architecture, CPU family or hypervisor. Our goal is to ensure that Ubuntu users can select whatever platform they want for their workloads and know they have access to the very best performance and efficiency across the entire stack from kernel to codec.

If they wish, we will enable performance and correctness engineers to move between products every two years, so that they have the opportunity to raise the bar for performance in an array of products over time, and also that teams have the benefit of fresh eyes on their processes, thinking, harnesses, dashboards and code. Our performance and correctness leads are expected to be truly exceptional individuals, and also leaders who are confident setting expectations of change, sharing insights and skills, running initiatives and programs. There is no way to move a meaningful codebase without also moving the people behind it.

This is a career path for perfectionists and precision artists. Whether you have a particular language focus - C, C++, Rust, Golang, Python, Java, Flutter-Dart or others - or a particular love of the kernel or hardware or CPU instruction set, whether you see yourself as driving perceived user experience through performance or optimising the efficiency of data centers to reduce carbon footprint, this process is the best way to find a role at Canonical that speaks to your precision, rigour, insight and drive.

jobs.description:
This global leadership role in cyber security is to manage the Security Operations (SecOps) team responsible for design, implementation and evolution of Canonical security practices, techniques, tools, systems and policies. The team is the primary owner of strategy and practices that determine how Canonical secures its data, internal infrastructure and build processes. They are responsible for assuring the security and integrity of our own infrastructure and product deployments. They design and implement technical security controls that ensure security threats are automatically identified, contained and remediated. The team will also contribute ideas and requirements for Canonical product security, improving the resilience and robustness of all Ubuntu customers and users subject to cyber attack.

As a leader on cyber security in the company, the SecOps team manager will collaborate with our Organisational Learning and Development team to develop playbooks and facilitate SecOps training across Canonical. They will operate in a wider security organisation, run a high performing security team and improve Canonical's security posture. They will lead initiatives to integrate the team's insights into Canonical's broader software development process.

While this is a management position, we expect managers to be expert practitioners, able to lead by example, contribute at the highest level, and assess work based on their own professional experience and skill. Candidates should have deep, hands-on expertise with a range of open source and proprietary security tooling and practices, which they can integrate into a holistic next generation security solution across the breadth of Canonical's interests.

The SecOps team's mission is not only to secure Canonical, but also to contribute to the security of the wider open source ecosystem. They might share knowledge through public presentations and industry events, and share threat intelligence with the wider community or represent Canonical in sector-specific governance bodies.

This role reports to the CISO.

What you will do in this role:

jobs.description:
This is a general track role, hiring for opportunities across all levels of seniority in our Sales Teams.

Apply here if you believe you possess outstanding revenue generating experience from the Technology industry. 

Open source software is the new default in the enterprise, and Canonical is the new challenger to major enterprise software vendors.

We deliver better open source from the data center to cloud and edge. Our Linux distribution Ubuntu is now the leading platform for public cloud compute, and the favorite platform for software engineers, data scientists and AI developers. Our mission is to accelerate the adoption and quality of open source globally, and our goal is to ship the most software on the planet by cores. A tidal wave of open source innovation is the next phase of the entire enterprise software industry, and we aim to be the most compelling way to ride that wave.

Our customers include Global 500 enterprises and startups. We are expanding our product range from the base operating system - Ubuntu - to full enterprise solutions in infrastructure and applications. We can deliver software defined storage, private cloud solutions, container runtime environments, as well as databases, message queues, identity, observability, analytics, machine learning and web publishing capabilities. Customers love the idea that they can get security compliance and support for everything open source from a single company. Our goal is to have more solutions on tap than any other vendor, and we have built unique capabilities to make that possible across every cloud, every class of compute and every category of application.

Canonical provides licensed enterprise software products, commercial support, managed services, consulting and training services to customers who are deploying Ubuntu or open source applications on the cloud, in their data center, or to the connected device and IoT ecosystem. We are just over 1,000 colleagues in 70+ countries and $250m in revenue, profitable, on a steady but relentless growth trajectory. We are almost entirely distributed, with leadership spread across many countries. We believe that talent is equally distributed across the globe, and we are excited to hire, develop, promote and ultimately trust a diverse group of exceptional leads to build the best, not biggest, enterprise software company.

We hire carefully and deliberately; our selection process is long and requires substantial work from applicants. It will take successful applicants three to six months to secure an offer. This opportunity is designed for early-career researchers with standout recognition, ready to drive progress on significant open problems and influence the future of AI research.

  1. Identify and propose an impactful open problem or theoretical bound within your research subfield for targeted investigation.
  2. Develop and execute sustained research strategies using advanced AI agents on tasks such as proofs, algorithmic innovation, and computational simulations.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Standout early-career achievements, including at least one best paper award at a premier venue (e.g., STOC, FOCS, SODA, PLDI, SC) or a recognized dissertation/early-career award; proof of recognition is required.

Each package is a new part you design from scratch: a difficult, high-value CNC part with a specific machining challenge, backed by a drawing with full GD&T, a design rationale, and a production scenario you justify from experience.   1. Design original parts in parametric CAD, delivered as native files plus STEP.
  2. Produce the technical drawing: dimensions, tolerances, GD&T and datums, material and condition, finish, revision, drawing standard.
  3. Write the design context: intended function, interfaces, operating conditions, the machining challenge, and your material and process rationale.
  4. Build the production scenario: estimated unit cost and drivers, CNC cycle and setup hours, assumed volume, sourcing difficulty and lead time — with the engineering basis for each estimate.
  5. Peer review other engineers' packages against technical quality, production realism, and engineering value, with part-specific evidence for every score.
  6. Revise your own packages against review findings.

What we're looking for

  1. 5+ years of production engineering experience with comparable CNC parts, materials and processes in aerospace or space hardware.
  2. Technical decision authority: you owned or approved critical design choices — drawing, tolerance or material approval, production release, or enforcing engineering quality standards. Design leads, principal and staff engineers, and technical authorities are the profile.
  3. Experience at OEMs or suppliers whose engineering standards you can reproduce.
  4. Strong GD&T and tolerancing judgment, including cost and inspection implications.
  5. Access to parametric CAD software (SolidWorks, NX, CATIA, Creo or similar) and the ability to deliver native files plus STEP.
  6. Industry experience, not academic.

How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions

You dream of a new challenge, of being able to make a company scale and feel that you have a real impact.

If you dream of a life that is more like an adventure than a stable life, then becoming the AI-native right hand of our CEO is for you.

This isn’t another chief of staff or right hand job.

Most companies call themselves AI-first because they gave everyone a ChatGPT licence. We think that’s level 2, and there are 10.

At Paradox our ambition is $10M in revenue with 10 people, each of them running a dozen agents. Here, AI doesn’t assist the work. It runs the loops, in every department. Your job is to make that true for the whole company, side by side with the CEO.

But wait a minute.

Deep inside you are looking for a new adventure with…

  • 🗽Freedom: working remotely or hybrid, and being trusted to deliver

  • 🔥Ambition: building one of the first truly AI-native companies, with teammates who push AI to its limits every week

  • 😍Impact: changing the trajectory of a whole company, not one line of a roadmap, with a product that transforms people’s lives at scale

Then, you have found the next adventure that will fulfill you.

WHAT AI-NATIVE MEANS AT PARADOX 🤖

In a company of fewer than 10 people, the right hand used to be the person who absorbed everything the CEO couldn’t do. Here, the right hand builds the machine that does it.

Our company has to be able to:

  1. Hold the full context of Paradox. Our DNA, offers, decisions, procedures, member stories and past experiments, in one shared company brain that every person and every agent reads before acting.

  2. Turn every decision into execution. A meeting, a voice note or a call with the CEO becomes briefs, tickets, follow-ups and deadlines, without anyone retyping it.

  3. Act across every tool. Not a chatbot in a tab: agents read and write in our whole stack, from code to CRM, billing, analytics, ads, email, calendar and documents.

  4. Ship. Produce the analysis, the contract draft, the page, the offer or the process, and put it live.

  5. Measure with real KPIs. Revenue, cash, margin, retention and the transformation of our members, not activity.

  6. Learn and loop on its own. Keep what works, kill what doesn’t, write the lesson back into the brain, and start the next cycle without waiting for a meeting.

People set the ambition, the taste and the standards. The machine runs the loop, and gets better every week.

This is already real. Our company brain holds our decisions and procedures. Our growth hub tracks every hypothesis and experiment with its result. Agents cut ads from long-form content, prepare webinars and audit our tracking after every live. And our product is AI-native too: Athena, our AI coach, works with members every day, by text and by voice.

But maybe YOU WONDER WHAT’S OUR STORY? 😉

We believe self-help is broken. Most people use learning platforms the same way: generic theory, a quick high, no real change.

They deserve more than content and more than motivation.

They deserve a system that knows them, one that adapts, challenges and grows with them.

That’s why we merge:

  • Human Intelligence (coaches, peers and mentors)

  • Structured Intelligence (protocols, mental models, rituals)

  • Technological Intelligence (AI personalization, feedback loops, adaptive journeys)

into one seamless ecosystem: Paradox OS, the Operating System for Human Greatness, augmented with AI.

Paradox was founded by David Laroche, a creator followed by over 2 million people and known for his interviews with icons like Tony Parker, Mike Horn, Richard Branson and Gad Elmaleh. We started in French. We’re building for the world, and for something that will outlive any individual, its founder included.

Here’s the bet: A small team running a self-learning machine can out-test, out-learn and out-grow teams a hundred times its size.

And that’s where you come in.

YOUR MISSION 🚀

Reporting directly to the founder and CEO, you will help him run and grow the company.

Your scope is as wide as a CEO/COO’s: strategy, operations, finance, legal, people, product marketing and launches.

The difference is how you do it. In a classic company, the right hand coordinates people and AI helps. Here it’s the other way round: agents do the work, you design the system, set the bar and make the calls. With fewer than 10 people, there is no department to hand things to. You build it.

🎯 YOUR 5 MAIN MISSIONS

1 - Be the CEO’s operating system

  • ❌The old way: a chief of staff takes notes in meetings, chases people by email and builds the weekly report by hand.

  • 🏴‍☠️At Paradox: you build the agents that turn every CEO decision into execution. Meetings, voice notes and calls become briefs, tickets and follow-ups. Every Monday, the CEO gets one brief: what moved, what’s stuck, and what needs his call.

  • You decide what the CEO must see and what he never needs to see again. His time goes to vision, product and members, not to coordination.

2 - Run strategic projects as a Pirate Squad of one, plus agents

Depending on your zone of genius, these are examples of strategic projects you could own:

  • Growth: run experiments with agents that generate, ship and measure them

  • Partnerships & sponsorships: find and close partners aligned with our brand, for our YouTube channel and events

  • International: build the machine that turns our French content into English, and open new countries

  • Launches: take a new offer or product from idea to live

  • People: find and assess the rare people who join a team of fewer than 10

  • ❌The old way: each new initiative needs a team, a roadmap and three months.

  • 🏴‍☠️At Paradox: one person with the right agents launches an offer, a channel or a country without disrupting the core. That’s what our Pirate Squad means now.

3 - Build AI-native operations

  • ❌The old way: an ops manager processes invoices, chases contracts, onboards people and answers the same support questions every week.

  • 🏴‍☠️At Paradox: finance, legal, HR, admin and customer support each get their agents, their context, their KPIs and their loop. You write the skills, plug them into our tools and write the evals that define "good": a reconciliation that matches to the cent, a contract that respects our playbook, an answer a member is happy with.

  • You give autonomy step by step: first an agent suggests, then it acts once you approve, then it acts alone within a budget and guardrails. An agent moves up a level only when its track record earns it.

  • Example: in your first month, you build the agent that reconciles payments, refunds and failed charges every night. In month one it only reports. By month three it fixes the simple cases alone, and you only see the exceptions.

4 - Strategy and business intelligence that check themselves

  • ❌The old way: someone builds dashboards in a BI tool, exports them to a spreadsheet at the end of the month, and nobody fully trusts the numbers.

  • 🏴‍☠️At Paradox: agents watch revenue, cash, acquisition, retention, churn and competitors continuously, find where our sources disagree, and explain what changed and why.

  • Strategy: screen markets and competition, build growth models, explore business models, partnerships and acquisitions. Then challenge, formalize and ensure good execution of the strategy.

  • At Paradox things move fast, and our CEO is always reading business books and meeting great entrepreneurs. You’ll turn the best strategies and tactics into systems and agents the whole company uses.

5 - Make the machine better every week, and keep the soul

  • ❌The old way: lessons live in people’s heads and leave with them.

  • 🏴‍☠️At Paradox: every decision, result and lesson goes back into the company brain, and agents read it before acting. The company never learns the same lesson twice.

  • You measure the machine itself: the share of work done without a human, the time from decision to execution, the agents that moved up an autonomy level this month, and revenue per person. You push those numbers up.

  • You help the team become AI-native too: you spot the work still done by hand, and you build the agent or show a teammate how to build it.

  • And always: our members trust us with their lives. No fake claims, no fake scarcity, data handled with care. The machine can scale, but it doesn’t decide what’s right. People do.

How you’ll know you’re AI-native: you spend your time building agents, writing evals and making calls, not doing the work by hand. The company’s output grows every month while the headcount doesn’t.

DO YOU RECOGNIZE YOURSELF? 😍

Experience

  • Top tier Business or Engineering School (HEC, ESSEC, INSEAD, EM Lyon, EDHEC, ESCP, Stanford, …) or other high-level academic training (Les Mines, X, Sciences Po Paris, etc.)

  • A wide-scope role behind you: founder, chief of staff, founder’s associate, strategy, consulting or operations in a fast-growing startup

  • You’ve built with AI and agents yourself: Claude Code, agent SDKs, MCP, automations, APIs, evals. Show us something you built, not a certificate.

Traits

  • Driven with strong work ethic: this position requires a strong commitment and perseverance

  • Entrepreneurship spirit: able to own a project from scratch, with few resources and little guidance, doing a lot yourself

  • Builder, not coordinator: you’d rather build the agent than chase a person twice

  • Taste: you know the difference between an output that works and one that is great, and you hold agents to the second

  • Growth over ego: you are at ease with regular feedback, obsessed with learning and growing, able to put your ego aside

  • Analytical and system thinker: you quickly identify and formulate problems, and solve complex ones with data

  • Excels in communication: both written and verbal

Language

French: native or bilingual. English: fluent, you can hold a detailed conversation with English-speaking colleagues. Our chosen language for written communication is English.

IT MIGHT NOT BE FOR YOU

  • We are inspired by a culture of performance and ambition. Everything is fast-paced and there is a lot of change. You won’t always be told what to do or how to do it.

  • We tell each other things, even if they are uncomfortable. We value growth over ego. At Paradox, expressing disagreement to a manager and knowing how to debate is valued! We encourage critical and strategic thinking.

  • ❌ If you use AI for first drafts but your way of working looks the same as two years ago: wrong role.

  • ❌ If you want to manage a lot of people: we aim for $10M in revenue with 10 people, each managing a dozen agents.

  • ❌ If you need clarity before chaos: wrong place.

If all this makes sense with you, then we’ll love working with you (and you with us, you’ll be pampered!)

WHY JOIN US ❤️

Build one of the first truly AI-native companies from inside the CEO’s office, and write the playbook others will copy. You’ll compete with San Francisco companies.

A work with Impact, Freedom and Ambition

Growth & Ambition 🚀

  • 🏅Being surrounded by A-players who strive to perform, whilst being in a good mood

  • 🏋️‍♀️No more bosses, but ongoing conversations to support your growth

  • ⚡️Learning to build with AI faster than almost anywhere else

Impact & Meaning 🔥

  • 🦄Playing a crucial role in the development of a company whose content and products are used by millions of people

  • 🤩Waking up in the morning feeling like you are making a difference is something! We receive messages every day from members who quit smoking, reached a milestone in their business, built better relationships and changed their lives.

But that’s not all, we believe that driven people deserve…

Freedom & Well Being 🗽☀️

  • 😎A company culture based on autonomy & accountability

  • 🗽Flexible working hours (but very hard working)

  • 🌎A remote culture from day one with the freedom to work from wherever you want

  • 🧍‍♀️Standing desks paid by the company if you live far from our offices

  • 💻Work on Mac

  • 🏀350€ per year paid by the company to take care of yourself (for your gym, a dance class or whatever makes you feel great)

  • 📚150€ of books or education: at Paradox, we are learner lovers

  • 🔥Access to Athena, our AI coach, supporting you on anything personal or professional

HOW TO APPLY 📃

❌ Any copy-pasted and non-personalized application goes directly to the trash can.

⚠️ To complete the recruitment process, each candidate must organize calls with his or her previous managers. If you are not comfortable with this: do not apply ⚠️

Hiring process

  • 📃 A 6 to 8 minute application survey, with a short video and a link to something you built with AI

  • 💻 A 30-minute video call with Timy, HR, to deep dive into your career path and ambitions

  • 🛠️ A live build session: you solve a real Paradox problem with AI in front of us. We look at how you prompt, push back on the output and iterate, more than at a polished result.

  • 💻 A 1h culture-fit video call, to assess alignment with our values and mindset

  • 💻 A 1h final video call with David, CEO, on the company’s next milestones and how you’d build them

  • 💼 Reference calls with your previous managers

  • 🤗 Welcome aboard!

If all this sounds good to you, come and write the next chapter with us 🚀🚀

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer — AI Architecture Research
jobs.description:
About the Role

We’re looking for a Machine Learning Engineer focused on AI architecture research to help design, prototype, and validate next-generation model architectures. You’ll work at the intersection of research and production — turning new ideas into scalable, real-world systems.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys questioning architectural assumptions, experimenting with novel model designs, and pushing beyond standard Transformer-style approaches.

What You’ll Work On

  • Research and develop new neural network architectures (e.g. alternatives or extensions to Transformers, recurrent / hybrid models, long-context systems)

  • Design and run architecture-level experiments (scaling laws, memory mechanisms, compute trade-offs)

  • Prototype models end-to-end — from research code to training-ready implementations

  • Collaborate with inference and systems engineers to ensure architectures are deployable and efficient

  • Analyze model behavior, failure modes, and inductive biases

  • Read, reproduce, and extend cutting-edge research papers

  • Contribute to internal research notes, benchmarks, and open-source efforts (where applicable)

What We’re Looking For

  • Strong background in machine learning fundamentals and deep learning

  • Hands-on experience implementing model architectures from scratch

  • Solid understanding of:

    • Attention mechanisms, RNNs, state-space models, or hybrid architectures

    • Training dynamics, scaling behavior, and optimization

    • Memory, latency, and compute constraints at the model level

  • Comfortable working in PyTorch or JAX

  • Ability to move fluidly between theory, experimentation, and engineering

  • Clear communicator who can explain architectural trade-offs

Nice to Have

  • Experience with non-Transformer architectures (RNN variants, SSMs, long-context models)

  • Background in research-driven startups or open-source ML projects

  • Experience with large-scale training or custom training loops

  • Publications, preprints, or notable research contributions

  • Familiarity with inference optimization and deployment constraints

Why Join

  • Work on core model architecture, not just fine-tuning

  • Direct influence on the technical direction of a Series-A company

  • Small, high-caliber team with fast feedback loops

  • Opportunity to ship research into production

  • Competitive compensation + meaningful equity

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer — Training Optimization
jobs.description:
About the Role

We’re looking for an ML Engineer focused on training optimization to help us scale and improve large-scale model training. You’ll work at the intersection of research and production, optimizing training pipelines for speed, stability, and cost—while collaborating closely with researchers pushing model architecture and capability forward.

This is a high-impact role with real ownership: your work directly affects how fast we can iterate, how large we can scale, and how efficiently we deploy new models.

What You’ll Do

  • Optimize large-scale model training pipelines (throughput, convergence, stability, and cost)

  • Improve distributed training strategies (data, model, and pipeline parallelism)

  • Tune optimizers, schedulers, batch sizing, and precision (bf16 / fp16 / fp8)

  • Reduce training time and compute cost via profiling, bottleneck analysis, and systems-level improvements

  • Collaborate with researchers on architecture-aware training strategies

  • Build and maintain robust training infrastructure (checkpointing, fault tolerance, reproducibility)

  • Evaluate and integrate new training techniques (e.g. gradient checkpointing, ZeRO, FSDP, custom kernels)

  • Own training performance metrics and continuously push them forward

What We’re Looking For

  • Strong experience training large neural networks (LLMs or similarly large models)

  • Hands-on experience with training optimization (not just model usage)

  • Solid understanding of:

    • Backpropagation, optimization algorithms, and training dynamics

    • Distributed systems for ML training

  • Experience with PyTorch (required)

  • Comfort working close to hardware (GPUs, memory, networking constraints)

  • Ability to move fluidly between research ideas and production-ready code

Nice to Have

  • Experience with large-scale distributed training (multi-node, multi-GPU)

  • Familiarity with DeepSpeed, FSDP, Megatron, or custom training stacks

  • Experience optimizing training on AMD or NVIDIA GPUs

  • Contributions to open-source ML infrastructure or research codebases

  • Exposure to non-Transformer architectures (RNNs, hybrid models, etc.)

Why Join Us

  • Real ownership at Series-A stage — your work shapes the company’s trajectory

  • Work on cutting-edge models and training systems at scale

  • Small, highly technical team with fast feedback loops

  • Strong emphasis on engineering quality and research rigor

  • Competitive compensation + meaningful equity
